sentences.text:
The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Petition No.1856 Of 2022
O R D E R:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioner - accused to quash the proceedings in C.C.No.392 of 2019 pending on the file of learned Judicial I Class Magistrate, Tandur.
The offences alleged against the petitioner are punishable under Sections 420, 406, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respondent - State.

3. On the basis of private complaint filed by the 2nd and 3rd respondents, the learned Judicial I Class Magistrate, Tandur, has taken on file the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of IPC, against the petitioner.

The said order dated 24.06.2019 reads as follows:
"This Court on oral enquiry of the complainant 1 and 2 and the documents filed in support of their contention.
Cognizance is taken under Sections 420, 406 IPC against the accused.

4. As seen from the order dated 24.06.2019 passed by the learned Magistrate, wherein cognizance was taken against the petitioner, the order does not reflect that the learned Magistrate has grasp the case and nothing is mentioned in the case regarding the facts, which prompted the learned Magistrate to take cognizance, except stating that documents were taken into consideration.

Since,
there are no details of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to set aside the order taking cognizance, in view of the orders passed by this Court in Crl.P.No.3777 of 2023.
However, this Order will not preclude the learned Magistrate from taking cognizance by stating reasons.
5. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.

K.SURENDER, J Date: 21.04.2023 rev Sri. Ram Prakash vs The State Of Telangana on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10709800/
